intended_object: The end construction as a functor from the bifunctor category, (Jᵒᵖ ⥤ J ⥤ C) ⥤ C. It sends F to its end ∫_j F(j,j) and a natural transformation to the induced map on ends. Here the ends are the ones fixed by a `ChosenEndsOfShape J C` instance. This is read off the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation: On objects, the functor sends F to `chosenEnd F`, the apex of the chosen limiting wedge. On morphisms, it sends a transformation f : F ⟶ G to `chosenEnd.map f`. That map is the unique lift whose j-th component is π_j ≫ f_{j,j}, which is the standard functoriality of ends. The lemmas `map_id` and `map_comp` are proved just above, so the `Functor` structure is well defined. The construction works for any categories J and C, which is the natural generality; it only assumes that ends of shape J are chosen. It is the chosen-data analogue of Mathlib's `endFunctor`, which is defined under `HasEnd` through `end_`, so it agrees with the textbook end functor.
